the spatial distribution of Alzheimer pathology in the brain is not uniform and that the rate of spatial change in NFT is a significant predictor of cognitive change in the elderly.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial distribution of NFTs and NPs in the human brain is highly ordered, and that this order can be quantified and modeled using LGC techniques.
the spatial gradient of neurofibril tangles is the best predictor for Braak staging, while the gradient of neuritic plaques is the best predictor of APOE e4 burden.

the spatial pattern of NFT is a major determinant of the spatial pattern of cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease, but the spatial pattern of NP does not appear to be a major determinant of cognitive decline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LGC modeling is a powerful tool that can be applied to spatially ordered data.
LGC models can be used to estimate the regional distribution of pathology and to quantify its variability across individuals.
the spatial pattern of Alzheimer's pathology is highly variable across individuals, even when controlling for age and APOE e4 burden.
